name: astral-3d
description: The Thermo Astral analyser: an asymmetric-track multi-reflection time-of-flight instrument, modelled entirely from published information. Two elongated mirrors face each other across a 40 mm board gap; ions oscillate between them while drifting along their length, and the mirrors converge slightly so the drift decelerates and reverses. Each mirror is a two-dimensional cross-section whose extrusion axis is tilted by half the convergence, which makes the field anisotropy Ez/Ex exactly tan(alpha) instead of a quantity no affordable three-dimensional mesh can resolve - see docs/astral-handoff.md sections 12 and 13. The two solves carry one mirror at potential with the other grounded, which is the ordinary basis decomposition and therefore exact. The ion foil is not included: its shape is measured in section 11 and the drift force it produced was 5.7 times what the published reversal needs, so it is a study rather than part of the shipped device. The third element is the ion foil: a volume solve carrying the four shaped plates at their graded bias with every mirror strip grounded, which is the basis field psi_foil. It supplies most of the drift reversal - mirror tilt alone is 31 to 38 per cent of what the published reversal needs, and the exact impulse law forbids any electrode design from changing that.

ionEnergy.description: Nominal beam energy. Stewart et al.: 4 keV entering the analyser.

spacerThickness.description: Thickness of the spacer that tilts the mirrors relative to one another. PUBLISHED: Stewart et al. give 200 microns. What it is not published over is the baseline - see tiltBaseline - and that is the whole of the uncertainty in the drift reversal.

tiltBaseline.description: Length the spacer tilts each mirror over, so the tilt angle is asin(spacerThickness / tiltBaseline). GUESSED, and it is the most consequential unpublished number in this model: 250 mm reproduces every published reversal figure (334.76 mm of drift, 25 reflections, 13.39 mm per reflection against a published 310 to 360, 24 to 26, 13.40) while reading the 200 microns as closing the GAP across the 350 mm drift instead gives 714.81 mm and 61 reflections. The two readings differ by 2.8x in the tilt. Handoff section 17.

injectionAngle.description: Tangent of the angle between the trajectory and the mirror axis, setting the drift rate as V tan(theta). 0.03998 is 2.29 degrees, which is what the published drift distance and oscillation count imply through D/N = t_r V tan(theta) / 2 - a relation containing no convergence term, so it fixes the angle independently of whatever decelerates the drift. Stewart et al. state "about two degrees". Handoff sections 14 and 17.

driftLength.description: Extent along the drift. Published 310-360 mm.

capToCap.description: Cap plate to cap plate. Derived, not published, and derived a second time on 2026-09-01 because the first derivation was wrong. Stewart et al. give 24 to 26 oscillations over a flight path exceeding 30 m, so one oscillation is 1.154 to 1.250 m. An oscillation is out and back between the two turning points, so their separation is 577 to 625 mm - and that is NOT the cap-to-cap distance, because the ion turns short of the cap. Measured here, the turning point sits 84.2 mm past the mirror mouth and that offset is independent of capToCap, as it must be: the turning depth is fixed by the potentials and d1..d4. So separation = capToCap - 2 (mouth - 84.2) = capToCap - 91.6 mm, and 24 oscillations over 30 m needs capToCap = 716.6. The original 625 mm was the separation mistaken for the cap-to-cap distance, and it made the analyser 15% short in path and so 15% short in drift per reflection.

boardGap.description: Board-to-board separation at the drift mid-point.

boardThickness.description: How thick each board is in y.

vacuumPad.description: Vacuum between the outermost metal and the solve boundary.

detectorInset.description: How far inside the far end the collecting plane sits.

d1.description: Depth at which U1 is reached, from the mirror mouth. FREE: no paper states the electrode lengths, and they are what the published coefficients were optimised against.

d2.description: Depth at which U2 is reached, from the mirror mouth. FREE: no paper states the electrode lengths, and they are what the published coefficients were optimised against.

d3.description: Depth at which U3 is reached, from the mirror mouth. FREE: no paper states the electrode lengths, and they are what the published coefficients were optimised against.

d4.description: Depth at which U4 is reached, from the mirror mouth. FREE: no paper states the electrode lengths, and they are what the published coefficients were optimised against.

mouth.description: Where each mirror opens toward the beam.

detectorZ.description: kept for reference: where a detector at the FAR end of the drift would sit. The shipped detector is behind the launch point instead, because an asymmetric-track analyser's ions drift out, reverse, and come back - catching them at the far end measures only the outbound half and hides the behaviour the device is named for.

mirrorTilt.description: Tilt of each mirror, in half turns. The near stack takes +mirrorTilt and the far -mirrorTilt, which brings both mouths toward the mid-plane as z increases.

zPad.description: how far the solve domain and the electrode stripes run beyond the drift at each end. The reversal convergence moves 7.4% from 0 to 50 mm and 0.4% from 50 to 150, so this is converged; at zero the Neumann face sits 10 mm from where the ion turns round.

foilVolts.description: Foil bias at the injection end. PUBLISHED range 0 to -20 V. Shipped at 0, so the foil element contributes exactly nothing and the reversal is the mirror tilt alone, which is what the detector paper says does it. The foil geometry is kept because its published job - countering the time-of-flight aberration the converging mirrors induce - is the open problem, and the profile that does it is an optimisation this model has not run. Handoff sections 16 and 17.

foilThickness.description: how thick the foil electrodes are.

foilGap.description: Half-gap between the foil plates in the board-gap direction. Defaults to halfGap, so the foil is a shaped conductive region on the inner face of each board rather than a separate aperture in the flight path - which is both the plausible construction for a printed-circuit analyser and what the published schematic projects to. Mounting the plates flush costs 15% of the well depth (7.31 V against 8.58 V at foilGap 8 mm) and leaves the well shape unchanged, shallowest at 41% of the drift and deepest at 67%.

foilSlices.description: Number of constant-width boxes the contoured foil plate is built from. The contour runs along the drift, so each slice spans a range of drift and holds one inner-edge position.

foilOuterFrac.description: Foil plate outer edge, as a fraction of the mid-plane to mirror-mouth distance. Measured from the published schematic at 146 mm of 182 mm; the outer edge is straight to within one pixel over the whole drift.

foilInnerMid.description: Mean position of the foil plate inner edge, as a fraction of the mid-plane to mirror-mouth distance. The inner edge is contoured along the drift; this is the midpoint of that contour.

foilInnerAmplitude.description: Half the peak-to-peak excursion of the foil inner edge along the drift. The published schematic gives 0.641 of the reach at the plate thinnest and 0.515 at its thickest.

foilThinAt.description: Drift fraction at which the foil plate is thinnest, so its inner edge lies furthest from the axis and the gap between the two plates is widest.

foilThickAt.description: Drift fraction at which the foil plate is thickest, so its inner edge lies closest to the axis and the gap between the two plates is narrowest. Half a contour wavelength past foilThinAt.

foilStartFrac.description: Drift fraction at which the foil begins. The published figure shows the plates starting about a quarter of the way along, and that is what section 11 measured - but a foil that starts late cannot reverse the drift at all, because the net work a conservative axial field does is q(phi_start - phi_end) and an ion that crosses the whole potential bump nets nothing. Set to zero so the foil spans the drift and the ion begins inside it. Handoff section 15.

foilReach.description: Distance from the analyser mid-plane to a mirror mouth, the scale the foil plate positions are expressed as fractions of.

foilOuter.description: Foil plate outer edge, measured from the mid-plane.

foilDriftSpan.description: Fraction of the drift the foil covers.

foilGrade.description: How far the foil bias is graded along the drift. 0 biases every slice at foilVolts; 1 grades linearly from foilVolts at the injection end to zero at the far end, which is a resistor chain. The grade is what makes the deceleration the right SHAPE: both settings reverse the drift once the foil spans it, but graded gives 12.70 mm of drift per reflection against a published 13.40 and uniform gives 18.30.

convergence.description: How much the cap-to-cap gap narrows across the drift length. DERIVED from the spacer and its baseline, and reported because it is the quantity the earlier revisions of this template declared directly. 0.56 mm at the shipped values.

maxX.expression: midPlane - (foilInnerMid + foilInnerAmplitude * cosPi(((foilStartFrac + foilDriftSpan * (slice + 0.5) / foilSlices) - foilThinAt) / (foilThickAt - foilThinAt))) * foilReach
midPlane - (foilInnerMid + foilInnerAmplitude * cosPi(((foilStartFrac + foilDriftSpan * (slice + 0.5) / foilSlices) - foilThinAt) / (foilThickAt - foilThinAt))) * foilReach

minX.expression: midPlane + (foilInnerMid + foilInnerAmplitude * cosPi(((foilStartFrac + foilDriftSpan * (slice + 0.5) / foilSlices) - foilThinAt) / (foilThickAt - foilThinAt))) * foilReach
midPlane + (foilInnerMid + foilInnerAmplitude * cosPi(((foilStartFrac + foilDriftSpan * (slice + 0.5) / foilSlices) - foilThinAt) / (foilThickAt - foilThinAt))) * foilReach
